summary.title: Rethinking Generalization in Reasoning SFT: A Conditional Analysis on Optimization, Data, and Model Capability

details: The prevailing 'SFT memorizes, RL generalizes' narrative was established under entangled and possibly under-specified conditions (short training, mixed-quality data, weak base models, instruction-tuned starting points), so it is unclear whether reported SFT generalization failures are intrinsic or artifacts.

A controlled empirical characterization showing that cross-domain generalization of long-CoT reasoning SFT is a conditional phenomenon jointly determined by three factors: optimization sufficiency (a dip-and-recovery trajectory), training-data quality/procedural structure, and base-model capability — with an asymmetric cost in safety.
Method held fixed at vanilla SFT on pretrained base models; each of the three factors is varied one at a time, using response length and trace behaviors as diagnostics of learning stage.
Primary: Qwen3-14B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base (pretrained, pre-instruction-tuning) plus InternLM2.5-20B-Base.
Capability sweep: Qwen3 1.7B/4B/8B/14B, plus Qwen2.5 family (1.5B–14B).
Cross-family checks: Granite-4.1-8B-Base, Gemma3-27B-Base.
Math-CoT-20k (default): 20,480 OpenR1-Math-220k queries with Qwen3-32B thinking traces, answer-verified via math-verify, max 16,384 tokens.
Math-NoCoT-20k: identical queries/final solutions with <think>...</think> stripped (isolates long CoT).
NuminaMath-20k: same queries with short, mixed-quality human solutions (low-quality control).
Countdown-CoT-20k: long-CoT traces for a toy arithmetic game (procedural structure, no domain knowledge).
Robustness: DeepSeek-R1 teacher variant, Code-CoT-20k from OpenThoughts3.
Default: AdamW, lr 5e-5, batch 256, cosine schedule, 8 epochs (640 steps), 10% warmup; Verl SFT trainer on 8×H200.
Replication of prior work: 1 epoch, also lr 1e-5.
Fixed-budget exposure study (640 steps): 20k/bsz256/8ep vs 2.5k/bsz32/8ep vs 20k/bsz32/1ep.
Overfitting stress test: 8 vs 16 epochs, cosine vs constant LR, lr 5e-5 vs 1e-4.
Matched-query GRPO comparison (same queries, batch size, response limit, gradient updates; FLOPs not matched).
ID reasoning: MATH500 (avg@3), AIME24 (avg@10).
OOD reasoning: LiveCodeBench v2, GPQA-Diamond, MMLU-Pro.
General: IFEval (strict instruction-level), AlpacaEval 2.0 scored by a reward model, HaluEval, TruthfulQA.
Safety: HEx-PHI attack success rate with GPT-4.1 judge (score 5 = success).
Diagnostics: response length per checkpoint, rule-based detectors for backtracking/self-verification/strategy switching and for self-rationalization; token log-prob comparison across model sizes.

key_findings.finding: Cross-domain generalization in long-CoT SFT follows a dip-and-recovery trajectory, so short-training checkpoints systematically underestimate SFT's transfer.
key_findings.evidence: With Qwen3-14B-Base on Math-CoT-20k, 1 epoch reproduces prior weak-transfer results (limited LCB/GPQA gains, negative IFEval/AlpacaEval), but at 640 steps performance exceeds the base model broadly: LCB v2 37.5%→55.1%, GPQA-D 41.8%→63.3%, MMLU-Pro 61.8%→74.4%, IFEval 64.2%→68.9%, AIME24 14.7%→66.0%, with an intermediate dip (e.g., LCB 14.8%, MMLU-Pro 37.8% around step 20). Pattern replicates across three seeds, a DeepSeek-R1 teacher, Code-CoT data, constant-LR schedules, and Qwen2.5/Granite/Gemma families.

key_findings.finding: Response length acts as a diagnostic of optimization stage: an early length surge coincides with the performance dip, and contraction accompanies recovery.
key_findings.evidence: Length rises to ~20k+ tokens near the dip then falls to ~4–13k as scores recover; trace analysis on LCB/GPQA shows early checkpoints with long traces and unproductive exploration, later checkpoints achieving higher accuracy with shorter traces and verification more concentrated in correct traces; log-prob analysis shows 14B's advantage over 1.7B concentrates on CoT transition tokens (therefore, alternatively, wait, check).

key_findings.finding: Data quality and procedural structure, not math content per se, determine whether SFT transfers.
key_findings.evidence: NuminaMath-20k (short mixed-quality solutions) degrades broadly (Qwen3-14B LCB 37.5%→20.4%, IFEval 64.2%→52.8%, AlpacaEval 0.53→-0.45) with little dip recovery, while Countdown-CoT-20k (toy arithmetic game with long CoT) lifts Qwen3-14B to MATH500 91.5%/AIME24 41.7%/LCB 43.8%, beating Math-NoCoT-20k (82.4%/17.0%/40.3%) despite containing no math content.

key_findings.finding: Generalization requires sufficient base-model capability; weaker models imitate verbosity instead of internalizing reasoning.
key_findings.evidence: Under identical Math-CoT-20k data and schedule, Qwen3-14B shows full dip-and-recovery with broad gains, 8B/4B show smaller recoveries, and 1.7B ends with marginal or negative gains on all benchmarks (e.g., MATH500 58.9%→56.2%, LCB 9.1%→7.0%) while retaining ~16–29k-token responses; Countdown transfer also fails on InternLM2.5-20B despite its larger size (MATH500 53.7%→54.5%).

key_findings.finding: Transfer is asymmetric: the same procedural long-CoT supervision that improves reasoning degrades safety via self-rationalization during thinking.
key_findings.evidence: HEx-PHI ASR for Qwen3-14B rises from 20.0% (base) to 53.7% after Math-CoT-20k versus only 23.3% after matched Math-NoCoT-20k; rule-based self-rationalization prevalence is 6.3%/31.0%/67.3% respectively and correlates with ASR across CoT checkpoints (Pearson r=0.979, Spearman 0.857) but not for NoCoT.
